title: Falling OATs And A Divided France
gist: This is a paywalled teaser of roughly 200 words, not a full report: the available text is entirely a personal anecdote about the author's service as a second lieutenant in the French army's Mountain Infantry Division during the professionalization of the French military, and his then-support for ending conscription. The headline promise of falling OATs (French government bonds) and a divided France is never reached in the accessible text, so the framing — that France's social and military cohesion is the lens through which to read its bond market — can only be inferred from the title plus the setup.

insights.claim: The end of French conscription is framed as an unambiguously good thing at the time it happened, on the logic that high-tech warfare requires volunteer professionals rather than reluctant one-year draftees.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: The past tense of 'At the time, I was a big supporter' signals the piece is building toward a reversal — a rethink of conscription's civic role — which is the likely bridge to the 'divided France' argument behind the paywall.
insights.quote: if France was to have the best army she could have, then that army needed to be run by professional soldiers. The end of conscription was clearly a good thing.
insights.locator: At the time, I was a big supporter

insights.claim: The French army's transition to a professional force is presented through a Foreign Legion veteran NCO whose career spanned Gulf War I, Africa, Yugoslavia and Guyane, positioning expeditionary experience rather than mass mobilization as the model that replaced the draft.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Colour rather than tradeable signal, but it establishes the author's first-hand standing on French defence policy — relevant as European rearmament and any return of national service become fiscal questions for OAT issuance.

insights.claim: The accessible text of this Gavekal piece stops before any discussion of French government bonds, so the linkage between falling OATs and a divided France asserted in the headline is unsupported by anything readable here.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Do not treat this record as a source of a French rates view; the substance sits behind the sign-up wall and would need the full article before acting on any OAT positioning.

insights.claim: Opening a French sovereign bond argument with military conscription implies the author's causal chain runs from social cohesion and shared national obligation to fiscal and political stability, rather than from conventional deficit or ECB mechanics.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: If cohesion is the transmission channel, watch French political fragmentation and any debate over restoring national service as leading indicators for OAT spreads, not just budget headlines.
insights.locator: Falling OATs And A Divided France
